result.rationale: The diff replaces `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` with `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by an unconditional `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. When destinationCalendar is null or empty (as built in handleNewBooking: `destinationCalendar: ... : null`), the destructured value is undefined and the member access throws a TypeError, whereas the old optional-chained code handled the no-calendar case. This is a real crash regression on a previously-working path.

judged_text: The null-safe access evt.destinationCalendar?.integration was replaced with an unconditional member access on a destructured element, so mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws when destinationCalendar is null or an empty array. Every booking whose CalendarEvent has no destinationCalendar (the evt is built with destinationCalendar: null in handleNewBooking when neither eventType nor organizerUser has one) now crashes with a TypeError inside EventManager instead of skipping the Google Meet fallback check — a regression on the previously-working no-calendar path.

Every booking whose CalendarEvent has no destinationCalendar (the evt is built with destinationCalendar: null in handleNewBooking when neither eventType nor organizerUser has one) now crashes with a TypeError inside EventManager instead of skipping the Google Meet fallback check — a regression on the previously-working no-calendar path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the code now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then unconditionally reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in the Meet fallback check. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this throws a TypeError. The diff also shows `handleNewBooking` can set `destinationCalendar: ... : null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, so this path is reachable and is a regression from the prior null-safe `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` check.
